title: Health is becoming a continuous consumer practice spanning food, routines, data, devices, services and trusted human guidance
source_unit: PwC Voice of the Consumer 2026, The rise of everyday health
geography: 21,808 adults across 27 countries and territories, surveyed February-March 2026

observations.period: February-March 2026; global consumer health and wellness survey

denominator.unit: adult consumers surveyed across 27 countries and territories

continuous_practice.value: consumers report regularly buying for, tracking and adjusting health behaviors across food, sleep, stress, weight, appearance, performance and longevity

digital_use.value: 80% use an app or wearable for at least one health and wellness activity

market_shift.value: health is described as less episodic and institution-led and more continuous, personalized and woven into daily routines

observations.method: PwC global consumer survey, executive interviews and proprietary consumer-market analysis.
observations.uncertainty: The survey measures reported behavior and purchase interest, not verified health behavior, clinical outcomes, spending receipts or causal effects of digital tools.
observations.subgroup: Adult consumers across 27 markets, health-and-wellness shoppers, app and wearable users, older and younger consumers, providers, retailers and consumer brands.
observations.counterinterpretation: Health tracking may reflect experimentation or aspiration rather than sustained behavior; reported digital use does not establish effective or safe self-management.

observations.period: 2026; consumer interest in health products, services and data-enabled support

denominator.unit: adult consumers surveyed across 27 countries and territories

interest.value: consumer interest reaches 63% for health insights and diagnostics, 60% for coaching and behavior change, 54% for devices/equipment/smart environments, and 48% for lifestyle, environment and sensory tools

value_constraint.value: value for money is the leading attribute when consumers consider health-supporting products and services, with ease of use and clear information also important

platformization.value: products are increasingly wrapped in monitoring, guidance, subscriptions, diagnostics and personalized prompts

observations.method: Survey questions on future purchase interest and product/service categories, combined with PwC market interpretation.
observations.uncertainty: Interest and intended purchase are not realized adoption; category definitions and commercial framing may influence how respondents interpret the options.
observations.subgroup: Consumers with different budgets and health goals, retail and consumer-packaged-goods firms, digital-health providers, pharmacies and data-enabled service platforms.
observations.counterinterpretation: High interest can coexist with affordability barriers, privacy concerns, low trust or limited clinical usefulness; platform bundles may increase recurring costs and dependence.

observations.period: 2026; AI, wearables and first-contact health information

denominator.unit: adult consumers surveyed across 27 countries and territories

regional_ai_use.value: roughly one-third of respondents in the United States, United Kingdom and Germany use AI at the start of a health or wellness question; this rises to 61% or more in Asia, 68% in Latin America and 75% in the Middle East

human_influence.value: 57% cite healthcare professionals among the strongest influences on health actions, compared with 18% naming AI or conversational AI among their top five influences

data_trust.value: consumers are most comfortable sharing detailed health data for personalization with pharmacies, followed by insurers and fitness or training companies

observations.method: Cross-market survey of health-information behavior, technology use, influence and data-sharing comfort.
observations.uncertainty: Regional comparisons may reflect sample composition, question interpretation, access, health systems and cultural norms; reported comfort is not actual consent or data-sharing behavior.
observations.subgroup: Younger and older consumers, AI users, wearable users, patients, carers, healthcare professionals, pharmacies, insurers and consumer technology firms.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI may be used for exploration while people still rely on human experts for action; this does not imply that trust in professionals is stable or evenly accessible.

observations.period: 2026; consumer archetypes and unequal participation in the health market

segments.value: the five segments are data-driven optimisers (20%), value-seeking optimisers (17%), social wellness seekers (14%), holistic harmonisers (13%) and low-engagement consumers (35%)

access_gradient.value: the first four groups tend to be younger, more financially secure, more engaged with health technology and more willing to share health data; the low-engagement group skews older and responds to simplicity, affordability and trust

cultural_signal.value: wellness is simultaneously an individual optimization project, a value-and-budget calculation, a social belonging practice and a platform-mediated data relationship

observations.method: PwC cluster analysis of survey responses on product interest, behavior, attitudes, motivations and influences.
observations.uncertainty: These are proprietary analytical segments rather than fixed social identities; they describe survey patterns and do not establish stable populations or causal consumer types.
observations.subgroup: Younger and older consumers, financially secure and budget-constrained households, social wellness participants, data-oriented users and low-engagement consumers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Segment labels can encourage commercial targeting that overstates differences, obscures structural healthcare access and turns unequal resources into individualized lifestyle categories.

related_sources.claim: PwC publication page with the survey frame, consumer health findings, archetype analysis and methodology.
PwC survey methodology identifies the February-March 2026 field period, 21,808 adults, 27 markets and health/wellness question domains.

boundary: This record adds a consumer-health and platformization route linking daily routines to wellness spending, data, devices, AI, diagnostics, coaching, pharmacies, trust and affordability. It is a commercial survey and market-insight publication, not clinical evidence, verified purchasing data, a representative population-health study, a causal evaluation or proof that consumerized health improves outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official PwC publication page was reviewed for the 21,808-person/27-market survey frame, continuous health routines, app and wearable use, category interest, regional AI use, human influence, data-sharing comfort and five proprietary archetypes.
